article_content: Archaeologists have made a significant discovery in Galloway, uncovering evidence of a potential 'lost' Dark Ages kingdom. The findings suggest an alliance between the Britons and Picts, with the discovery of a Pictish carved stone and African pottery indicating a high-status individual, possibly a king, inhabited the site. The Picts were a fierce tribe known for their blue body-paint and hostile attitude towards southerners, while the Britons were a Celtic people who occupied much of Britain.

article_content: A search is underway for a missing Nepali sherpa, Chuwang Nima, who has successfully summited Mount Everest 19 times. Chuwang Nima Sherpa went missing after an avalanche occurred on Saturday, according to the mountaineering agency he works for. An avalanche swept Chuwang Nima away on 7,129-meter-high Mount Baruntse on Saturday afternoon while he was fixing ropes for climbers at 7,045 meters. 'Chuwang Nima was fixing ropes for another expedition on the mountain because they requested help when the avalanche struck,' said Jiban Ghimire of Sherpa Shangri-La Treks and Expeditions. Chuwang Nima was climbing with US mountain guide Melissa Arnot from Idaho. The two had planned an alpine-style climb without support staff, fixed ropes, or stops until the summit, Ghimire said. A helicopter was dispatched to search for Chuwang Nima on Sunday morning but had to return due to bad weather. Chuwang Nima, 39, is well-known in mountaineering circles and climbs and trains in the US. He was in Denali National Park in Alaska for technical training and rescue operations during the summer, according to Ghimire. Apa Sherpa, a 50-year-old Nepali, holds the record for summiting Everest, with 20 climbs. Everest is the world's highest mountain above sea level, at 8,848 meters.

article_content: Former Premier League referee Mark Clattenburg may be in for a surprise when he sees his colleague Dirk Kuyt's latest social media post. Kuyt, who has been linked with a move back to the Premier League with Southampton, showcased his impressive Kung Fu skills in a recent tweet. However, this might stir up some unpleasant memories for Clattenburg. The referee was involved in a controversy with Kuyt back in 2007 when he failed to give the Dutchman a red card for a Kung Fu-style tackle on Everton's Phil Neville. Clattenburg had earlier given a red card to Everton's Tony Hibbert, but changed his mind after a brief conversation with Steven Gerrard. It's worth noting that Clattenburg didn't referee another Everton match until 2012. If Ronald Koeman gets his way, Clattenburg might have the chance to officiate a match involving Kuyt again, as the Southampton boss is keen on bringing the 34-year-old back to the Premier League in January. article_content: The UK housing market has experienced a notable decline in young homeownership, primarily driven by rising house prices. According to research, in 1991, more than a third of 16-25 year olds owned their homes, but by 2011-12, this proportion had decreased to just one in 10. This trend is largely attributed to the difficulties faced by first-time buyers in obtaining loans, with the average age of first-time buyers now at 30. The Office for National Statistics identifies the main cause of this issue as the increasing demand for housing, combined with a low supply of new homes, leading to higher asking prices.
